# Your own listings and what each sold: trade/Listings.lua (FM.ListingsRecord, FRV-103) and its port ListingsBook in
# addons/ForeverMarket/tools/fm_analyze.py (FRV-125) read every case and must reach the outcomes below
# (tests/forevermarket/listing_outcomes_test.lua, tests/tools/test_listings.py). One character, "Tester"; now = minute 400000
# since the stamps' epoch; ago = minutes before now; an item's name is "item:<key>".
#
#   case <name>
#   post <ago> <key> <units> <unit price> <hours 2|8|24> <kind i|c> [auction ID]
#   event <osold|opart|ocancel|ogone> <key> <ago> <units> <buyout> <auction ID|-> <ago of the list before|-> [s]
#   mail <key> <ago> <total>                       a sale mail of one unit
#   expiry <key> <ago> [count]                     an expiry mail ("item:<key> (count)")
#   list <ago> [aid:key:units:buyout:status:secondsLeft ...]   your auction list, read then
#   expect <key> <n> sold <units> expired <units> cancelled <units> open <0|1>   the n-th post of the key, in log order
#   proven <key> <units> <ranOut 0|1> sold72 <units>

case commodity-false-sold-lines
# 155 at 5s: opart 1, 24 and 54, osold 130 at the unit price twice (the list's mark), the expiry mail of 23, ogone 23
post 1800 850 155 500 24 c c1
event opart 850 1700 1 500 c1 1710
event opart 850 1600 24 500 c1 1610
event osold 850 1500 130 500 c1 1510
event osold 850 1400 130 500 c1 1410
event opart 850 1300 54 500 c1 1310
expiry 850 355 23
event ogone 850 300 23 500 c1 310
expect 850 1 sold 132 expired 23 cancelled 0 open 0

case commodity-nothing-part-cancelled-sold-out
post 1800 851 120 500 24 c c1
event osold 851 1500 120 500 c1 1510
event ogone 851 300 120 500 c1 310
expiry 851 360 120
post 1800 852 80 500 24 c c2
event osold 852 1700 80 500 c2 1710
event opart 852 1600 70 500 c2 1610
event osold 852 1500 10 500 c2 1510
expiry 852 370 10
event ogone 852 300 10 500 c2 310
post 1800 853 102 500 24 c c3
event opart 853 1700 4 500 c3 1710
event opart 853 1600 26 500 c3 1610
event ocancel 853 1500 72 500 c3 1510
post 1800 854 100 500 24 c c4
list 300
expect 851 1 sold 0 expired 120 cancelled 0 open 0
expect 852 1 sold 70 expired 10 cancelled 0 open 0
expect 853 1 sold 30 expired 0 cancelled 72 open 0
expect 854 1 sold 100 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 0

case commodity-over-without-a-list-since
# over by the clock, your auction list last read before its end: running with what is known to have sold
post 1800 854 100 500 24 c c4
event opart 854 1700 30 500 c4 1710
list 1600
expect 854 1 sold 30 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 1

case commodity-purchase-entries
# 120 at 5s: opart 105, 9 and 4; an osold of 51 whose buyout is one purchase's total; running, then over
post 120 855 120 500 24 c c1
event opart 855 90 105 500 c1 80
event opart 855 60 9 500 c1 50
event opart 855 30 4 500 c1 20
event osold 855 20 51 25500 c1 10
post 1800 856 120 500 24 c c2
event opart 856 1770 105 500 c2 1760
event opart 856 1740 9 500 c2 1730
event opart 856 1710 4 500 c2 1700
event osold 856 1700 51 25500 c2 1690
list 60
expect 855 1 sold 118 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 1
expect 856 1 sold 120 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 0

case item-merely-gone-running-in-the-newest-list
# d1 gone from a list while you were away but running in the newest one; d2 a sold row the list showed
post 600 861 3 1000 24 i
event osold 861 500 1 1000 d1 510
event osold 861 480 1 1000 d2 490 s
list 400 d1:861:1:1000:a:50000
expect 861 1 sold 1 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 1

case item-posts-of-one-minute
# two posts of the same item and price in the same minute, 3 mails: the post logged first takes its 2 first
post 600 862 2 1000 24 i
post 600 862 2 1000 24 i
mail 862 590 1000
mail 862 580 1000
mail 862 570 1000
expect 862 1 sold 2 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 0
expect 862 2 sold 1 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 1

case commodity-two-parts-of-one-size
# 10 at 5s (FRV-118): a list shows the running 5 and sale A's row of 5; the other 5 sell to one buyer (sale B) after
# A's mail went out, so the next list shows only B's row. Since 1.40.6 the writer logs B as an osold line of its own
# (the same nth as A's), and B's line comes again after a list that lacked its row; the auction list was read after
# the post's end: sold out. Until 1.40.6 it logged the rest of 5 as cancelled (the second post, the same sales)
post 1500 870 10 500 24 c c1
event osold 870 1400 5 500 c1 1410 s
event osold 870 1300 5 500 c1 1310 s
event osold 870 1200 5 500 c1 1210 s
post 1500 871 10 500 24 c c2
event osold 871 1400 5 500 c2 1410 s
event ocancel 871 1300 5 500 c2 1310
list 30
expect 870 1 sold 10 expired 0 cancelled 0 open 0
expect 871 1 sold 5 expired 0 cancelled 5 open 0
